_photo_role: driver claim whose photo is a byte-for-byte copy of PS-02 photo1

dispute_ticket.description: After this trip the rear floor mat was covered in mud and I had to take the car for cleaning. I ask for S$75 from the rider.

chat_logs.content: I wore clean office shoes. There was no mud in your car.

app_events.details: Rider R-6045 booked trip RYDE-PS-009 from Suntec City to Blk 52 Marine Parade Central.
Driver submitted cleaning claim S$75.00 with 1 photo and a cleaning receipt.
Receipt attached: Sparkle Auto Care, Ubi Ave 1, S$75.00, dated 2026-10-13 17:00.

cleaning_fee_max.text: The maximum cleaning fee in SGD that may be charged to a rider for one trip. The fee is paid to the driver.

cleaning_fee_tiers.value: food or drink spill up to S$40; stains (mud, dirt) and bodily fluids up to S$120; vomit up to S$200
cleaning_fee_tiers.text: Usual fee by type of mess; a fee above the tier for the mess type needs a receipt.

cleaning_claim_evidence_required.value: photo of the mess and a cleaning receipt where available
cleaning_claim_evidence_required.text: Evidence a driver must provide to support a cleaning fee claim against a rider. It governs driver cleaning claims only.

photo_window_after_dropoff_min.text: A cleaning claim needs at least one photo of the mess taken within 60 minutes after drop-off, at or near the drop-off point.

photo_doubt_rule.text: If a photo's authenticity, timing, place or content is in doubt, a case officer decides; the fee is neither confirmed nor removed automatically.

rider_may_dispute_if.text: Lists the grounds on which a rider may dispute a cleaning fee charged to them.

evidence.description: Mud on the rear floor mat after drop-off at Marine Parade.

expected_outcome.reason: The photo submitted for this 13 Oct trip (RYDE-PS-009) is a byte-for-byte copy of photo1.jpg already filed by the same driver D-6377 on dispute PS-02 / trip RYDE-PS-002 on 5 Oct, so it cannot show a mess from this trip. The rider denies any mess. A receipt for S$75 is attached but the photo is a reused image, so its authenticity and timing are in doubt. Under this trip's photo-doubt rule a case officer decides; the claim is neither upheld nor dismissed automatically.
